highlights.title: Madison Huang, Jensen Huang’s Daughter, Became a Powerful Force at Nvidia
highlights.summary: Installed as her father’s de facto chief of staff, Jensen Huang’s daughter alienated top executives. Now her lingering role poses a test for interim C.E.O. Colette Kress.
body: Madison Huang was yelling. Her father, Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, had been scheduled to headline a conference in New Delhi in February. Shortly before the event, Mr. Huang pulled out and tapped a longtime lieutenant, Jay Puri, to attend in his place.

But Nvidia hadn’t buttoned up its plans for the conference, infuriating Ms. Huang. On a call ahead of the event, Ms. Huang berated other employees — including Mr. Puri — for being unprepared, said three people familiar with the meeting. Eventually, Mr. Puri interrupted and told Ms. Huang he could answer her questions if she stopped yelling at him.
Less than six months later, Mr. Puri left his role at Nvidia.

The tense meeting highlighted the powerful and sometimes disruptive role Ms. Huang, 35, played at the company her father co-founded, according to more than a dozen current and former employees who spoke on condition of anonymity about the family’s leadership of Nvidia. Before Mr. Huang resigned last week, she had become his de facto chief of staff, with considerable authority over more seasoned executives.

highlights.title: Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him
highlights.summary: Jensen Huang's stunning resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Now prominent figures are calling for Huang's reinstatement, and many are also hopping on board with a theory spreading throughout Silicon Valley: that the scandal is the…
body: David Sacks, Tim Sweeney, and other big names in tech are raising questions about the circumstances surrounding Huang’s resignation.

David Sacks, a venture capitalist and former White House AI crypto advisor, has made it clear that he’s skeptical about The New York Times ’ reporting. In a post on X, Sacks points to an article from CNN, which says US officials still can’t confirm that Alice Huang was a spy. “The spy narrative is collapsing already,” Sacks writes. He continued to question the spy allegations during Semafor ’s Silicon Valley & The World event on Monday, saying: “The reason why Jensen lost his job is because of this lurid Chinese spy allegation. So if no one’s willing to back that up now, then again, I question why this entire chain of events happened.”

highlights.title: Swansea braced to lose Vítor Matos as Strasbourg seek to replace Hugo Oliveira
highlights.summary: Matos has indicated a desire for move to Ligue 1. Championship club would be due compensation. Swansea City are increasingly resigned to their head coach, Vítor Matos, joining Strasbourg after he indicated a desire to join Chelsea’s sister club.
body: Strasbourg, acquired by Chelsea’s parent company BlueCo in 2023, have identified Matos as a replacement for Oliveira, who has won three of 10 league matches since succeeding Gary O’Neil in July. The French club are hovering two points above the relegation zone.
Matos is under contract until 2030 and Swansea would be due significant compensation for the 38-year-old, a former Liverpool academy and development team coach.

Matos has won admirers since taking charge of Swansea last November and, despite one win in their past five games, has the south Wales club in the Championship playoff spots. Swansea finished last season in 11th and backed Matos in the transfer market this summer in the hope of pushing on.
Swansea’s next match is at home to West Brom on Saturday, before a trip to Middlesbrough and a south Wales derby against Cardiff in the Welsh capital.

highlights.title: How 2026's Best Video Games Were Made
highlights.summary: Ahead of The Game Awards Game of the Year nominees, creatives behind Resident Evil, Control, Star Wars, and Pragmata pull back the curtain
body: What is great "game direction"? We love asking those in charge because everyone's answer is different.

Players' minds tend to jump to cinematic AAA blockbusters, where cutscenes and spectacle make the director's hand easy to recognize. But the beauty of video games is that greatness comes in endless forms. To prove out the point, Polygon assembled some of the creative minds behind 2026's most ambitious games to dig into what we believe remains a misunderstood art: the delicate balance of artistic vision, technical execution, and player experience that can transform a collection of ideas into a Game of the Year contender.
These wildly different philosophies all arrive at the same challenge: How do you make something that feels unmistakably your own while remembering that somebody actually has to enjoy playing it?

highlights.title: At Least Robert Pattinson Looks the Part…According to Ian Fleming
highlights.summary: The Bond author commissioned a sketch of 007 in the 1950s — and it bears an uncanny resemblance to a certain British actor currently being fitted for a tuxedo.
body: Well, it took nearly 70 years, and there were plenty of detours along the way, but Ian Fleming finally got the James Bond of his dreams — at least when it comes to jawline and nose shape.

Connery and Lazenby had dark hair but brown eyes. Craig had blue eyes but fair hair (controversial coloring that inspired more than a few cheeky headlines when he was cast: “No Mr. Blonde, They Expect You To Dye”). Moore had blue eyes but his hair was shades too light. Brosnan came closest, with black hair and blue eyes. But it turns out Fleming had other criteria aside from basic coloring and measurements.

In fact, the author commissioned a portrait of Bond in the 1950s, years before the movies were launched, when a British newspaper purchased the rights to serialize the novels as a cartoon strip. To help the paper’s illustrator nail down the look, Fleming hired an unknown artist to sketch 007’s face according to his highly specific instructions (“I think we should avoid giving Bond an American-shaped head and a duck’s haircut,” he wrote in one note).

highlights.title: Pilots Kept Contact With Controllers During Nationwide Halt to Flights
highlights.summary: Pilots were generally able to maintain contact with air traffic controllers and airline staff on the ground despite an outage that caused a nearly five-hour halt to departures.
body: Pilots were able to maintain communications with air traffic controllers and airline dispatchers during the nationwide halt to most departing flights imposed by federal officials for nearly five hours on Friday.

A representative of the union that represents about 17,000 pilots at American Airlines said on Monday that it had received no reports of crews losing radio contact with controllers. Some pilots noticed radio static, but that isn’t uncommon, said Dennis Tajer, a spokesman for the union, the Allied Pilots Association.
Even so, the union said it supported the hourslong ground stop called by the Federal Aviation Administration, a part of the Department of Transportation.
Southwest Airlines dispatchers, who help to plan and guide the carrier’s flights, also reported no disruption of direct communications or data before the ground stop was ordered.

highlights.summary: A humanoid robotics company backed and advised by President Donald Trump’s son, Eric Trump, has reportedly missed payroll and may be on the brink of collapse after a funding shortfall.
body: Foundation failed to pay employees for the payroll period ending on October 30, anonymous sources told CNBC. The startup’s staff is especially angry because Foundation’s co-founder and CEO, Sankaet Pathak, supposedly borrowed $4.6 million in company funds to buy a luxury home overlooking San Francisco Bay about a year ago.

This comes as Pathak and Foundation’s leadership are still looking to raise funding to support a $3 billion valuation, based on their promise to develop a humanoid robot ready for combat duty and capable of wielding various weapons.

The company has demonstrated a humanoid robot named the Phantom MK-1 and is touting an upcoming robot called the Phantom MK-2. Foundation has touted its humanoid robots for roles in warehouses and other workplaces—but has courted media coverage by claiming it is developing humanoid robots for battlefield use.
Now CNBC’s reporting based on “people with direct knowledge of the matter” indicates that insiders worry the startup could soon collapse without additional funding.

highlights.title: The open-source movement wants Jensen Huang back
highlights.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. On Friday, a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia began circulating on social media, and by Monday it listed some notable signatories, including…
body: These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. Supporters of such models say that concentrating AI in the hands of a few powerful companies will leave everyone else worse off (a concern that wouldn’t sound out of place among the AI industry’s critics on the left, if so many open-source advocates weren’t also venture capitalists who stand to profit when startups can build on cheaper AI without paying Big Tech).

Huang had become a sort of ringleader for those who defend open source to policymakers against concerns that such models come with no guardrails and cede AI leadership to China, where the most powerful and popular open-source models are created. They now want their most influential voice returned to his post.

But it’s not just Huang’s extramarital affairs that threaten his (and Nvidia’s) credibility as an advocate for open-source AI. New research into China’s startups using Nvidia’s chips, and a new rule from the US Department of Commerce announced Monday, could deal a blow to both the movement’s reputation and its technical progress.

body: A police raid has failed to locate three Melbourne Cup trophies belonging to champion horse Makybe Diva after a smash and grab at Flemington racecourse.
A Mount Waverley home in Melbourne’s east was raided on Monday evening after thieves smashed their way into a glass display case at the racecourse about 6.30am.
A 36-year-old Malvern East man was arrested at the Solomon Street home.
The trophies, which Victoria police says are valued at $1m each, are yet to be recovered.

highlights.title: UK’s National Health Service Is Urging Gamers to Protect Their Hands Ahead of GTA 6 Launch
highlights.summary: The UK’s National Health Service is giving players advice to help them avoid straining their hands once GTA 6 finally releases on November 19. The service’s humorous PSA was posted to Instagram on November 16, just three days before Rockstar’s highly anticipated game launches.
body: The poor employee explained that they underwent surgery to “remove a lump” from their hand, which they said is particularly “bad timing” due to GTA 6’s imminent release. To help others avoid injuring themselves and being unable to play, they shared some tips to keep your ligaments in tip-top shape.
The NHS’s post was particularly concerned with RSI, or repetitive strain injury, which it described as “pain that can be caused by repeated movement of part of the body, such as hands and fingers.”

RSI can happen for a number of reasons; sports like tennis or golfing can be culprits, as can jobs like hairdressing (using scissors and other tools), working an assembly line, and even typing at your computer.

While RSI is a general umbrella term for these types of injuries, carpal tunnel is a more specific condition that falls under the RSI label. Gamers are prone to this type of strain, due to pressing buttons quickly and repetitively, moving a joystick back and forth, and gripping one’s controller or mouse tightly while playing.

highlights.title: An Intriguing Approach to Slow Alzheimer’s Shows Mixed Results
highlights.summary: The device, a headset delivering light and sound, is based on the theory that audiovisual stimulation can evoke brainwave responses that might help preserve neurological function.
body: The largest trial to date of a headset device that delivers flickering light and sound in an attempt to slow the progression of Alzheimer’s has delivered mixed results.

Results of the study of the device, presented on Monday evening at a major Alzheimer’s conference, showed that the 12-month trial involving participants with mild to moderate Alzheimer’s did not achieve its primary goal. The overall group of patients who used the audiovisual device did not experience slower cognitive decline than those who used an inactive placebo device called a sham.

Patients with moderate Alzheimer’s showed no benefit at all from the system, called Spectris, according to data provided by the company, Cognito Therapeutics, which sponsored the trial. But for patients with mild Alzheimer’s, data generally suggested they could experience slower decline with the device, particularly if they used it nearly every day for close to the recommended 60 minutes.
Based on that, Cognito’s chief executive, Christian Howell, said the company planned to seek Food and Drug Administration approval.

highlights.title: Three small failures combined to take down Microsoft 365
highlights.summary: A hidden defect in Microsoft's cloud gateway, dormant since July, was to blame for one of the largest outages in the company's history last week. A preliminary Post-Incident Report (PIR) released by the company outlines how the latent bug, changes in traffic, and reduced server capacity combined to…
body: Microsoft’s preliminary report places the outage between November 12 at 16:20 UTC and November 13 at 16:10 UTC, just under 24 hours total, and additional monitoring remained in place for any affected systems through November 14.

The outage started on November 12 and quickly rippled through businesses and public offices that depend on Microsoft’s cloud and email exchange infrastructure. The outage is covered in Microsoft’s incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821. You need Microsoft 365 admin credentials to see the full report on the company’s status pages, but Office Watch has reproduced the preliminary report, and the University of Pennsylvania maintains an archive of Microsoft’s service-health updates.

Microsoft attributes the outage to three factors. A change deployed to Microsoft’s cloud gateway starting in July created a bug where, under certain conditions, CPU and memory resources could become exhausted and unresponsive. Microsoft contends that the defect was never discovered in pre-release testing because the hardware used was less powerful than some systems already deployed in production, where higher CPU core counts on newer machines apparently contributed to the lockout.

highlights.summary: We’re expanding our ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program to offer 200,000 researchers worldwide free access to our frontier models.
body: We’re expanding the ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program to give up to 200,000 researchers worldwide free access to ChatGPT.

The program began as a pilot in July. Applications for the next round open Monday, November 23. We’ll award 50,000 new grants to eligible researchers on a first-come, first-served basis. Each grant gives the recipient and up to two collaborators free access to ChatGPT Plus. If you’re already on the waitlist and qualify, we’ll email you before applications open with instructions for activating your account.
Participants can use OpenAI’s frontier models and get training on how to use ChatGPT in their research. By default, we don’t use data shared through the program to train our models.

highlights.title: 'Is that not match-fixing?' - Erasmus questions officiating
highlights.summary: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus predicts Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast will not face a ban after being cited, and questions standards in officiating.
body: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has predicted Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast will not face a ban after being cited, and questioned what he perceived as double standards in officiating to the point where he asked: "is that not match-fixing?"
Prendergast became the first player to be cited under World Rugby's new regulations for a hip-drop tackle against Fiji and could be banned for Saturday's Nations Championship match.

Speaking at a media conference on Monday, Erasmus said the 23-year-old's tackle was "terrible", but he believes Prendergast will be free to play against the Springboks in Dublin because of a "technicality".

The 54-year-old also added that he thought it was an "immediate red card" when he saw the tackle occur in the first half of Ireland's 43-15 win, but it was not penalised in-game by referee Angus Gardner or by the television match official Mike Adamson.

highlights.title: Hospitals Brace for Medicaid Work Rules and Deep Funding Cuts
highlights.summary: Eskenazi Hospital in Indianapolis is dispatching teams into the city’s low-income neighborhoods to help educate patients on keeping their Medicaid coverage.
body: Hospitals across the country are mobilizing an expansive outreach effort in an attempt to ensure that roughly 19 million patients do not lose their insurance coverage under new Medicaid work rules that begin in January.

Saying the requirements are generating widespread anxiety and confusion, health care executives are using a variety of methods to help guide the Americans who will be affected. They are deploying staff and volunteers to contact patients with text messages, phone calls and offers of help.

The rules dictate that able-bodied adults without young children either work, volunteer or attend school or job training for at least 80 hours a month. Republicans included the rules last year as part of President Trump’s package of tax cuts and reductions in safety net spending, including nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts.
Hospitals and other health centers are detailing what evidence people in many cases must provide — pay stubs or other proof of work or school attendance — to maintain coverage.

highlights.title: The Bank Outage May Have Nothing to Do With Your Bank
highlights.summary: Amid hundreds of reports of US banks experiencing outages, JPMorganChase says a technical “issue” with its “on-premise hardware systems” may be causing “slowness” with transactions at outside banks.
body: Customers of many major financial institutions experienced unspecified technical issues on Monday as thousands of reports flooded the uptime-tracking website Downdetector.com from people saying that they had issues using their banks in some way.

It is currently unclear which systems are having issues. However, the problem may stem from technical difficulties at JPMorganChase, the top retail bank that holds over 10 percent of all US deposits, did identify a specific issue.

“JPMorganChase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems—there is no evidence this is cyber-related,” says JPMorganChase spokesperson Pablo Rodriguez. “It is taking longer than usual to service some customers.”

Rodriguez adds that the bank is not experiencing a “systemic issue” but that “other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us.” The spokesperson adds that customers “still have access to their accounts and funds” and that the bank is working to resolve the issues.

body: So when Guardiola visited Yankee Stadium in September to serve as New York City FC’s pre-match hype man before their rivalry match with Red Bull New York, Pochettino – in town anyways to scout the match – made it a point to sit with him during the game. “You know what I noticed?” Pochettino asked, smiling as he recounted the story during a meeting with reporters on Monday. “[Guardiola had a] good relationship with JT.”

Back then, Pochettino didn’t seem to be going anywhere. Only a month earlier, he’d signed a four-year contract to guide the US through the 2030 World Cup. Guardiola was, and still is, in the middle of a year-long sabbatical from coaching. He remains the federation’s white whale, often mentioned in the same breath as the US job over the past decade-plus but just as quickly dismissed as a pipe dream.

Just three months after taking in that game at Yankee Stadium, Pochettino is on his way to Manchester United and Guardiola has once again found himself at the center of the rumor mill, with reports suggesting that he and US Soccer are set for exploratory talks.

body: The European Union has published a draft proposal for the DFA, calling for changes to in-game currencies to more clearly state their value, disclose loot box odds and give users ability to turn off loot boxes - with all IAPs disabled by default for minors.

Supercell has been a champion of the free-to–play mobile space since launching Hay Day and Clash of Clans back in 2012, making billions of dollars in the years since. It’s become one of the region’s most successful gaming companies.
Paananen said while the European Commission promises to protect consumers with new regulations, the opposite will happen.
He claimed that by making it harder for players to buy something, there will be fewer free games on the market. Around 95% of Supercell’s monthly players play for free.

“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” first arrived in cinemas on July 31 and skyrocketed as the summer’s biggest blockbuster success. The superhero tentpole debuted to $927 million worldwide on opening weekend and has since extended its global tally to $2.5 billion. Directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, the film is currently the third-highest-grossing movie of all time behind 2009’s “Avatar” ($2.92 billion) and 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.88 billion) and ahead of 2022’s “Avatar: The Way of Water” ($2.3 billion) and 1994’s “Titanic” ($2.2 billion).

highlights.summary: If your pillows are flatter than a pancake, it’s time to upgrade. From foam and latex to classic down, there is one here that’s right for you. Could these three pillows unseat my favorite? Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I t’s pretty common advice that you should invest in anything that connects you to the ground. Most people think of shoes, tires and mattresses. However, I think people overlook things such as socks and pillows. The humble pillow can spell the difference between a fantastic night’s sleep and tossing and turning until dawn.
Goldilocks and I are on the same page. You need a pillow that isn’t too soft, hard, cold or hot. It needs to be just right.

I have been testing and reviewing products for more than 13 years, including for the Guardian’s Filter US since October 2025, with items such as bath towels, dryer balls and space heaters. I got my start at a product-testing lab where I tested household products under a combination of established and bespoke standards, and I specialized in washing machines and fabric care, and helped develop sleep lab protocols. I’m all about making sure products live up to what is advertised on the tin and provide good value. Plus, I love naps.

A good pillow should be able to provide support without feeling hard and be soft without completely enveloping you. To test this, I placed a 20lb weight on each pillow’s center and measured the amount of compression.

highlights.title: Trump Administration Moves to Close A.I. Chip Loophole Ahead of China Trip
highlights.summary: The rules have been a topic of fierce debate in the administration and would cut back on a booming data center business serving Chinese companies.
body: The Trump administration said on Monday that it was moving forward with a new rule that would clamp down on China’s ability to access advanced A.I. chips through the use of data centers outside China’s borders.

The rule aims to close what many in Washington see as a loophole allowing China to sidestep a ban that prevents Chinese firms from buying the most advanced A.I. chips made by companies like Nvidia. Chinese firms have continued to legally access the chips by renting them from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere. Whether to close the loophole has been a significant source of contention within the Trump administration.

The new rule is intended to make it harder for Chinese firms to remotely access the chips. It will require overseas data centers to obtain a government license before supplying “significant volumes of computing power” to firms with headquarters in a small group of high-risk countries, a list that includes China, Russia and Iran.

body: Gerwyn Price and Luke Littler both made it through to the Grand Slam of Darts knockout stage on a night featuring a bizarre maths error and a sensational triple-bull checkout.

Price, meanwhile, claimed a 5-2 victory over Sebastian Bialecki - although he was the beneficiary of an unusual mathematical mistake.

highlights.title: Supercell and King bosses warn EU’s Digital Fairness Act could hurt players and studios
highlights.summary: King president Todd Green says Europe's 1,000-plus mobile studios face "dramatic consequences". UK trade body Ukie has also weighed in on the controversy.
body: Supercell boss Ilkka Paananen and King president Todd Green have hit back at the EU’s Digital Fairness Act, which the European Commission formally proposed on November 11.

The published proposal largely matches the leaked draft we reported on earlier this week. Paid-for virtual currencies would be switched off by default in games aimed at minors unless a parent approves, and loot boxes and pay-to-win mechanics would be banned for minors.

Games would also have to show the real-money value of virtual items, and let all players switch off loot boxes and addictive design features. In large-scale cases, the Commission would be able to fine companies up to 6% of their worldwide annual turnover.

The statements follow trade bodies Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation calling the proposal “unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate”, and warning that it would be “game over for the European games industry”.

highlights.title: Naming your feelings can be harder than you think. This simple tool can help
highlights.summary: About 10% of people have significant trouble identifying their emotions – which makes it harder to know what to do about them. Naming emotions is a core skill that most people develop as children, and it might seem like second nature.
body: That’s why a simple tool called the feelings wheel has gained popularity in therapists’ offices and classrooms over recent years.

At first glance, it looks a little like a pie chart: three concentric circles sliced into colored sections, with each region representing a different category of emotion. The innermost circle lists broad core feelings (sad/happy/angry), which split off into gradually more specific sub-emotions in the outer rings (remorseful/proud/humiliated).

Created by US psychologist Dr Gloria Willcox during the early 1980s, the feelings wheel is a tool designed to help people identify and clearly name their emotions, by moving gradually from broad blanket terms to more nuanced ones. The wheel has surged in popularity in recent years, thanks in part to its visual appeal – you can get it as a laminated office poster, as a wooden desk chart on a spin-stand or even stitched onto a cushion.

But do people really need this much help with the seemingly simple task of naming everyday feelings? Experts say that in many cases, the answer is yes – and behind this difficulty is an evidence-based scientific concept known as emotional granularity.
points: About 10% of people have significant trouble identifying their emotions – which makes it harder to know what to do about them.
Naming emotions is a core skill that most people develop as children, and it might seem like second nature.
That’s why a simple tool called the feelings wheel has gained popularity in therapists’ offices and classrooms over recent years.
